steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Appeasement was the policy of giving in to some of Hitler's demands in the hope of avoiding war. It was most associated with British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain (1937-1940), though it had been practised by earlier governments. The policy was based on the belief that some of Germany's grievances were legitimate and that negotiated concessions could satisfy Hitler and prevent another devastating war. | Key Fact: Appeasement was not simply cowardice or stupidity. It was a rational policy based on genuine concerns: war weariness, military unpreparedness, economic problems, fear of communism, and the belief that some German grievances were legitimate. | Key Fact: Neville Chamberlain became Prime Minister in May 1937 and made appeasement the cornerstone of British foreign policy

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain two reasons why Britain followed a policy of appeasement. (4 marks) | How far was appeasement justified? (8 marks) | "Appeasement was cowardly and misguided." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
